scope: Read-only official metadata search and manual review of two public source videos; no model inference, generated target, or active ABC input change.

pair_provenance.source_license: CC-BY-4.0 according to the official repository's License and disclaimer section; code Apache-2.0 is a separate license.
pair_provenance.instruction_author: Self-authored proposed diagnostic instructions, not official Perception Test editing annotations.

inspection.method: Inspected all eight CPU-generated contact sheets sampling every 15 original frames (approximately 2 fps), plus three full-resolution detail frames. This was sampled visual review, not continuous playback or frame-by-frame inspection.
inspection.exact_contact_timestamps: Per-video metadata.json records decoder PTS for every contact frame; detail seek times are requested times rather than certified exact output PTS.

official_selected_events.label: Pouring something from something into something

manual_observations: Indoor preparation scene. A person tilts a transparent bottle into a metal bowl around 15.7-17.2 s, then replaces/closes the bottle and stirs.
Around 24.8-26.3 s the person reaches to and moves the orange letter blocks beside the bowl. The full-resolution 25.5 s detail confirms orange blocks rather than paper pieces or cups.

The official viewer questions independently refer to the letters being shuffled; their reported starting order is asd and final order sad. Those question answers were checked as metadata, not independently read off every letter face.

A red container is also tilted earlier around 9.7-11.2 s. Official annotations label that event Pretending to pour from something into something, distinct from the later actual pouring event. This is an explicit ambiguity/distractor, not silently omitted.

Mixing occurs before and after the letter action; this is not a video containing only two isolated action blocks. The selected prompt constrains their relative order rather than the order of every action in the source.
sources.review_quality: Action order supported by official temporal labels and approximately 2 fps visual inspection. No claim of exact pixel/latent correspondence or complete continuous-playback verification.

official_selected_events.label: Pouring something from something into something

manual_observations: Outdoor preparation scene. The person moves small paper letter objects near the front of the table around 8.4-14.0 s. The full-resolution 10.7 s detail shows the paper letters being handled.

Afterwards the person lifts a small white bowl and tilts it into the larger metal bowl around 14.8-17.3 s. The full-resolution 16.3 s detail visibly shows a narrow yellow liquid stream; this is not inferred solely from container tilt.

The official viewer questions state that the letters end in their original order (to). Consequently the selected event means handling/shuffling the letters, not requiring that their final spatial order differ. The temporal test is the order of this action versus pouring, not the letters' left-right arrangement.
Earlier banana handling and later ingredient addition are also present. The selected actions are not truncated by the public file boundary and their annotated intervals do not overlap.
sources.review_quality: Action order and the liquid stream are supported by official annotations plus sampled visual review and full-resolution details. No claim of dense correspondence GT.

proposed_crossed_router_test.positive_label_definition: The source order of the two selected actions must change to satisfy the target relation while retaining both forward actions.
proposed_crossed_router_test.negative_label_definition: The source already satisfies the selected relative-order requirement, so the instruction does not require changing that order. This is not proof of exact same-frame correspondence in a generated output.

instructions.instruction: The liquid-pouring action should occur before the letter-handling action. Keep both actions and preserve the forward motion within each action, along with the person, setting, and objects.
The letter-handling action should occur before the liquid-pouring action. Keep both actions and preserve the forward motion within each action, along with the person, setting, and objects.

proposed_crossed_router_test.why_source_dependent: Each exact instruction has opposite labels on the two source videos; each source has opposite labels under the two instructions. A deterministic text-only or source-only classifier cannot classify all four cases correctly without additional source-order or instruction information.
proposed_crossed_router_test.text_only_balanced_expectation: With both sources weighted equally per prompt, a fixed prompt-only prediction gives 50% accuracy on the four crossed cases. This is a construction property, not a measured model result.
what_is_not_proven: No VLM has been run; neither its accuracy nor its benefit is established.
A VLM is not the only possible implementation: a reliable visual event recognizer plus an order comparator, or an accurate event transcript, could supply the needed source information.
Order already satisfied does not guarantee the generated target preserves timing, duration, or exact frame correspondence. That stricter claim needs output/correspondence evaluation.
Two different scenes with different letter-object forms are not a same-scene paired capture and do not establish broad benchmark generalization.
There is no official reference edited video, no approved 5-second derivative, and no generated GT. These long sources should not silently replace the current frozen ABC inputs.

recommended_next_step: Use the four proposed crossed cases first for an explicitly labeled source-dependent routing sanity check after selecting an authorized local visual model or other event-order observer. Continue looking for shorter same-scene natural sources or design and disclose derivatives separately. Do not infer VLM success or change frozen ABC jobs from this candidate review.
